tools.name: get_server_capabilities
tools.description: Use this when a client needs server capabilities: supported tools, datasets, population codes, recommended workflows, the live ClinVar release date, and current limitations. Returns ~7kB.

tools.name: get_variant_frequencies
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a CHROM-POS-REF-ALT id or rsID; returns a headline, exome/genome AC/AN/AF per population, and a summary (max_pop_af, faf95). Pair with get_clinvar_variant_details for clinical context. Compact defaults trim subcohort and zero-AC rows; toggle the boolean flags to expand, or use response_mode='full' for the most-inclusive breakdown or response_mode='minimal' for just the headline + overall/max-pop summary. summary.max_pop_af is the raw highest-AF ancestry group (may be bottlenecked asj/fin; never 'remaining') and is NOT the filtering AF: use summary.faf95.{exome,genome,joint}.grpmax (gnomAD faf95 at grpmax, continental groups only; kept in minimal mode; a source is omitted when gnomAD computed no faf95 for it, e.g. AC 0 there) as the ClinGen/Whiffin comparator. A `truncated` block reports rows dropped by filters. Returns ~2-4kB (minimal ~0.6kB).

variant_id.description: CHROM-POS-REF-ALT (e.g. 1-55051215-G-GA) or an rsID. Use M-POS-REF-ALT only with get_mitochondrial_variant.

dataset.description: gnomad_r4 (GRCh38, default, largest cohort), gnomad_r3 (GRCh38, whole-genome), gnomad_r2_1 (GRCh37 legacy)

populations.description: Restrict to these population codes (e.g. ['afr','nfe']). None returns all kept rows.

include_subcohorts.description: Include non_topmed_*, non_ukb_*, 1kg_*, hgdp_*, controls_* rows.

response_mode.description: compact (default) = today's behavior, honoring the include_subcohorts/include_sex_split/exclude_zero_populations toggles. full = most-inclusive population detail (subcohorts + sex-split + zero-AC rows). minimal = headline + overall/max-pop summary + _meta only (drops the exome/genome per-population arrays). response_mode='full' and response_mode='minimal' take PRECEDENCE over the explicit toggles above.

tools.name: get_variant_details
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a single variant id; returns transcript consequences, in-silico predictors, and exome/genome frequencies. This tool does NOT return ClinVar clinical significance — for that call get_clinvar_variant_details. Prefer get_variant_frequencies if only allele counts are needed. Compact trims the exome/genome population breakdown (drops subcohort, sex-split, and zero-AC rows; toggle the booleans to expand) and emits a `truncated` block per source. Returns compact ~3-6kB, full up to ~50kB.

variant_id.description: CHROM-POS-REF-ALT id (e.g. 1-55051215-G-GA) or an rsID. Use get_mitochondrial_variant for M-POS-REF-ALT.

dataset.description: gnomad_r4 (GRCh38, default, largest cohort), gnomad_r3 (GRCh38, whole-genome), gnomad_r2_1 (GRCh37 legacy)

response_mode.description: compact strips raw GraphQL extras and trims the population breakdown (see the toggles below); full passes through everything.

max_transcripts.description: Cap on transcript_consequences in compact mode.

populations.description: Restrict population rows to these codes (e.g. ['afr','nfe']). None keeps all kept rows.

include_subcohorts.description: Include non_topmed_*, non_ukb_*, 1kg_*, hgdp_*, controls_* rows.

tools.name: compare_variant_across_datasets
tools.description: Use this when a caller wants one variant's allele frequencies across gnomAD releases (r4 vs r3 vs r2_1); returns per-dataset AFs and the most divergent populations. Datasets that lack the variant are marked present=false (partial success); the GRCh37 gnomad_r2_1 leg is auto-lifted from the GRCh38 id. Pair with get_clinvar_variant_details for clinical context. Compact (default) drops the per-dataset population arrays (comparison.per_population_af_deltas keeps the per-pop AFs); response_mode='full' returns the raw rows. Returns ~2-4kB compact, ~3-8kB full.

variant_id.description: GRCh38 CHROM-POS-REF-ALT id (e.g. 1-55039974-G-T). r2_1 is auto-lifted to GRCh37.

datasets.description: Datasets to compare. None compares gnomad_r4, gnomad_r3, gnomad_r2_1.

populations.description: Restrict per-population rows to these codes (e.g. ['afr','nfe']). None keeps all.

auto_liftover.description: Lift the GRCh38 id to GRCh37 for gnomad_r2_1. Off skips r2_1 with a build note.

response_mode.description: compact (default) drops the duplicated per-dataset exome/genome population arrays (~half the payload) since comparison.per_population_af_deltas already carries every per-population AF; full keeps the raw ac/an rows; minimal returns the headline + per-dataset present flags + comparison.overall_af_by_dataset + _meta only (drops the raw per-dataset rows and per_population_af_deltas).

tools.name: compute_carrier_frequency
tools.description: Use this when a caller needs a Hardy-Weinberg carrier/affected frequency estimate from a single gnomAD allele frequency (AR, AD, or X-linked); returns a one-line `headline`, Wilson 95% CIs, per-population breakdown, and provenance (short citations + a gnomad://citations pointer in compact mode; full citations with response_mode='full'). Pure local math on top of get_variant_frequencies. Estimates are research-use only, never clinical decision support. Returns ~2-4kB.

inheritance.description: AR=autosomal-recessive (2pq carrier, q^2 affected); AD=autosomal-dominant (1-(1-q)^2); XL=X-linked (sex-split).

dataset.description: gnomad_r4 (GRCh38, default, largest cohort), gnomad_r3 (GRCh38), gnomad_r2_1 (GRCh37 legacy)

populations.description: Restrict per_population rows to these population codes (e.g. ['afr','nfe']). None returns all.

method.description: hwe = 2pq from AF; hom_corrected = (ac - 2*hom)/(an/2) observed variant carrier rate.

response_mode.description: compact (default) returns short citations + a citations_ref pointer to gnomad://citations; full inlines the complete bibliographic citations and assumptions prose; minimal returns the headline + global `overall` block + _meta (drops the per-population rows and full citations).

tools.name: get_gene_details
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a gene id or symbol; returns constraint scores (pLI/oe_lof), canonical transcript, and basic coordinates (chrom/start/stop only: gnomAD has no cytogenetic band; that is HGNC `location`, via hgnc_resolve_symbol). Follow with get_gene_variants if they then need per-variant rows. Returns compact ~2kB, full up to ~30kB.

gene.description: Gene symbol (e.g. PCSK9) or Ensembl gene ID (ENSG...).

reference_genome.description: Lookup build for gene coordinates and constraint. GRCh38 default.

response_mode.description: compact drops heavy arrays (transcripts, exons, alt_transcripts) and emits a truncated block; full passes through everything; minimal returns the headline + symbol/gene_id + pLI/oe_lof + coordinates + _meta only.

tools.name: get_gene_variants
tools.description: Use this when a caller wants per-variant rows for a gene (ENSG/symbol); returns each variant's id, consequence, HGVS, and AC/AN/AF. Caps large results at 500; consequence/AF/AC filters and include_populations control payload size. Reports cap use in `truncated` and describes retained population fields in `population_projection`. Returns ~5-45kB at the default limit=100.

gene_id.description: Ensembl gene ID or gene symbol.

dataset.description: gnomad_r4 (GRCh38, default, largest cohort), gnomad_r3 (GRCh38, whole-genome), gnomad_r2_1 (GRCh37 legacy)

consequence.description: Exact VEP major_consequence term to keep (e.g. 'missense_variant', 'stop_gained'); not a category like 'lof'. An unrecognised term is rejected as invalid_input, not zeroed.

max_af.description: Drop variants whose AF exceeds this threshold.

min_ac.description: Drop variants whose AC is below this threshold.

include_populations.description: Keep each variant's per-population breakdown (trimmed). Set False to drop the population arrays entirely (keeps ac/an/af) for a lean list scan — the biggest token saving.

include_subcohorts.description: Include non_topmed_*, non_ukb_*, 1kg_*, hgdp_*, controls_* rows.

exclude_zero_populations.description: Drop populations with allele_count == 0 from each variant.

tools.name: compute_gene_carrier_frequency
tools.description: Use this when a caller needs gene-level autosomal-recessive carrier frequency across qualifying pathogenic variants, not a single variant; returns global and per-population carrier frequency, genetic and Bayesian prevalence, a headline, provenance, and contributing variants. Run this server-side computation once per gene; do not loop over variants. Research use only; not clinical decision support. Returns ~4-30kB (gene/limit dependent).

gene.description: Gene symbol (e.g. CFTR) or Ensembl gene ID (ENSG...).

include_lof_hc.description: Count LOFTEE high-confidence LoF on the canonical transcript.

clinvar_star_threshold.description: Minimum ClinVar gold stars for a P/LP match.

include_conflicting_clinvar.description: Include conflicting ClinVar variants, resolved by P/LP submission share: 1 extra request per 24 variants, sent in turn; only the first 288 are resolved, the rest are counted in `degraded`.

conflicting_threshold.description: Min %% of P/LP submissions to accept a conflicting variant.

exclude_high_af.description: Drop variants with AF >= 0.05 (ACMG BA1) instead of flagging.

exclude_high_hom.description: Drop variants with excess homozygotes instead of flagging.

exclude_gnomad_filtered.description: Drop variants that failed gnomAD QC filters.

response_mode.description: compact caps the contributing-variant list; full returns all; minimal returns the headline + global block + contributing-variant COUNT + _meta (drops per-population rows and the contributing-variant list).

top_variants_limit.description: Cap on contributing variants in compact mode.

tools.name: get_gene_summary
tools.description: Use this when a caller wants a one-shot gene dossier: constraint (pLI/oe_lof), canonical and MANE-Select transcripts, top pathogenic ClinVar variants, and expression (mean pext + top GTEx tissues). Pass a gene symbol (e.g. PCSK9) or Ensembl gene ID (ENSG...). Use include_clinvar / include_constraint / include_expression to fetch only the sections you need (e.g. include_clinvar=false + include_constraint=false for expression-only). Follow with get_gene_variants for per-variant rows. Returns compact ~3-8kB (ClinVar-dependent); include_clinvar=false trims it most.

gene.description: Gene symbol (e.g. PCSK9) or Ensembl gene ID (ENSG...).

clinvar_limit.description: Cap on top_pathogenic ClinVar rows in compact mode.

include_expression.description: Include the best-effort expression block (mean pext + top GTEx tissues). False skips the extra GTEx upstream call.

include_clinvar.description: Include the ClinVar block. False drops it entirely (~10kB saved on ClinVar-dense genes) — combine with include_constraint=False for expression-only.

response_mode.description: compact ranks pathogenic ClinVar into clinvar_summary; full returns the raw clinvar_variants list AND the per-base pext regions; minimal returns the headline + top-line constraint + ClinVar pathogenic COUNT + _meta only. compact/minimal drop expression.pext regions (a truncated_pext marker with expression.mean_pext preserved); full retains them. All honor include_clinvar/include_constraint.

tools.name: get_clinvar_variant_details
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a single variant id; returns its ClinVar clinical significance, review status, gold stars, and submissions. Complementary to get_variant_frequencies for clinical workflows. Returns ~0.8kB per submission (default 25); lower submissions_limit for a smaller payload.

variant_id.description: CHROM-POS-REF-ALT id (autosomes, X, Y, M/MT), e.g. 7-117559590-ATCT-A. Match the build to reference_genome (GRCh38 default).

reference_genome.description: Lookup build for the variant id. GRCh38 (default) or GRCh37.

response_mode.description: Accepted for compatibility: both modes return the same payload. Every fenced text keeps raw_sha256 and provenance.retrieved_at.

tools.name: get_clinvar_meta
tools.description: Use this when a caller only needs the ClinVar release served by gnomAD; returns its release date, cheaper than full capabilities. Returns <1kB. DEPRECATED: prefer get_server_capabilities.

tools.name: compute_variant_liftover
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a variant id in one reference build; returns the equivalent id in the other. Works BOTH directions (GRCh37<->GRCh38); the converted coordinate is in each result's `target_variant_id` (and `target_reference_genome` names the build). Use this BEFORE calling frequency tools if the dataset and coordinate build do not match. Returns <1kB.

source_variant_id.description: Variant ID to convert (CHROM-POS-REF-ALT). Mitochondrial M/MT prefixes are accepted.

tools.name: get_region
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a small region (<=100kb); returns the genes and/or ClinVar variants in it. Spans larger than 100kb are clamped and a `truncated` block reports it. Per-category caps (`max_clinvar_variants`, `max_genes`) keep payload bounded; surplus rows are summarised in a `truncated_payload` block. For per-variant SNV listings use get_gene_variants instead. Returns ~5-30kB at compact defaults; up to ~50kB with compact_rows=False.

dataset.description: gnomad_r4 (GRCh38, default, largest cohort), gnomad_r3 (GRCh38, whole-genome), gnomad_r2_1 (GRCh37 legacy)

include_clinvar.description: Include ClinVar variants in the region.

compact_rows.description: Project clinvar/gene rows to a compact key set.

tools.name: get_coverage
tools.description: Use this when a caller needs gnomAD read-depth coverage for a gene, region, or single variant; returns per-position bins plus a {mean_coverage, fraction_over_20} summary, or scalar coverage for a variant. Pass ONE target — a gene symbol, Ensembl gene ID, region (chr-start-stop), or variant (CHROM-POS-REF-ALT) — and the scope is auto-detected. Compact mode trims each bin and caps bin count. Returns ~3-40kB compact (bin-count dependent), larger with response_mode='full'.

target.description: Gene symbol, Ensembl gene ID (ENSG...), region (chr-start-stop, span capped at 100kb), or variant (CHROM-POS-REF-ALT) for scalar per-variant coverage. The scope is auto-detected.

response_mode.description: compact trims each bin to pos/mean/median/over_20/over_30; full keeps all over_* thresholds.

max_bins.description: Cap on coverage bins per source (gene/region). Summary still reflects all bins.

tools.name: get_structural_variant
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a gnomAD structural variant id (DEL, DUP, INV, BND, CPX, MCNV); returns its type, coordinates, length, AC/AN/AF, and populations. SV ids come from search_structural_variants (search a gene/region first); they are NOT resolvable by resolve_variant_id, which is SNV/indel only. For SNVs/indels use get_variant_frequencies instead. Compact (default) drops heavy histograms + the duplicated flat gene list and emits a `truncated` block; response_mode='full' returns everything. Returns compact ~2-5kB; full ~10-20kB (histograms + populations).

variant_id.description: gnomAD SV identifier as returned by search_structural_variants (e.g. BND_chr12_e99836ac, DEL_chr1_1234abcd). Discover ids via search_structural_variants for a gene/region; do not guess the suffix.

dataset.description: Structural-variant dataset: gnomad_sv_r4 (GRCh38, default) or gnomad_sv_r2_1 (GRCh37).

response_mode.description: compact drops heavy age/genotype-quality histograms and the duplicated flat gene list; full returns the raw payload.

tools.name: get_mitochondrial_variant
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a mitochondrial variant id (M-POS-REF-ALT); returns its ploidy and heteroplasmy fields. For autosomal variants use get_variant_frequencies. By default zero-count heteroplasmy bins are trimmed and a `truncated.kind=heteroplasmy_zeros` block reports the count; set `include_heteroplasmy_zeros=True` to keep them. Returns ~2-4kB.

variant_id.description: Mitochondrial variant in M-POS-REF-ALT format. Accepts chrM-, MT-, and chrMT- aliases (normalized to M-).

dataset.description: gnomad_r4 (GRCh38, default) or gnomad_r3 (GRCh38); gnomad_r2_1 does not include mitochondrial variants

include_heteroplasmy_zeros.description: Keep zero-count bins in heteroplasmy_distribution histograms.

tools.name: get_transcript_details
tools.description: Use this when a caller has an Ensembl transcript id; returns its exon structure and (by default) a compact GTEx tissue-expression summary. GTEx is sourced via the gene path; the lookup is best-effort, so exon structure is returned even if expression is unavailable. For gene-level info use get_gene_details. Returns ~3-8kB (set include_expression=False to skip GTEx).

reference_genome.description: Lookup build for the transcript. GRCh38 default.

include_expression.description: Attach a compact GTEx tissue-expression summary (top tissues) for this transcript via the gene path. Set False to skip the extra upstream call and return only exon structure.

tools.name: search_structural_variants
tools.description: Use this when a caller wants structural variants overlapping a gene or region; returns SV rows (id, type, position, length, AC/AN/AF). Pass ONE target — a gene symbol, Ensembl gene ID, or region (CHROM-START-STOP) — and the scope is auto-detected. SV variant_id values are OPAQUE (e.g. DEL_19_1), NOT CHROM-POS-REF-ALT, so no SNV id grammar is applied; fetch a single SV by id with get_structural_variant. sv_dataset is the DISTINCT structural-variant dataset enum (gnomad_sv_r4=GRCh38 default, gnomad_sv_r2_1=GRCh37), not the SNV dataset. Type/length filters are applied client-side. An empty match is a success with returned=0, not an error. Returns ~3-30kB (limit-dependent).

target.description: Gene symbol, Ensembl gene ID (ENSG...), or region (CHROM-START-STOP, e.g. 19-11089000-11200000). The scope is auto-detected.

sv_dataset.description: Structural-variant dataset (DISTINCT from SNV datasets). gnomad_sv_r4 (GRCh38, default), gnomad_sv_r2_1 (GRCh37).

sv_type.description: Filter by SV class (uppercase enum). An unrecognised value is rejected as invalid_input.

min_length.description: Drop SVs shorter than this length (bp).

max_length.description: Drop SVs longer than this length (bp).

tools.name: search_genes
tools.description: Use this when a caller has a fuzzy gene query (symbol, alias, partial name); returns ranked matches with symbol, ensembl_id, and match_quality. Follow with get_gene_details for full constraint metrics. Note: gnomAD's gene autocomplete returns a bounded set and may omit exact members of a large gene family for a SHORT prefix (e.g. 'GRIN' does not return GRIN1/GRIN2B). If an expected gene is missing, query its FULL symbol (e.g. 'GRIN1') or call get_gene_details/get_gene_summary directly. Returns ~1-3kB.

query.description: Gene symbol, name fragment, or Ensembl ID.

reference_genome.description: Reference build to search gene symbols/ids within. GRCh38 default.

tools.name: resolve_variant_id
tools.description: Use this when the caller only has an rsID, a CHROM-POS-REF-ALT id to confirm, or text fragment; returns candidate canonical gnomAD variant ids. With enrich=True (default) the top hits include gene_symbol, major_consequence, and AF so the caller can rank candidates without a follow-up call. Mitochondrial ids (M-/MT-/chrM-POS-REF-ALT) resolve via the gnomAD mitochondrial dataset (gnomad_r4/r3 only) with af_hom/af_het; follow up with get_mitochondrial_variant. Returns ~1-5kB (enrichment dependent).

query.description: rsID, CHROM-POS-REF-ALT, or a chrM id (M-POS-REF-ALT).

dataset.description: gnomad_r4 (GRCh38, default, largest cohort), gnomad_r3 (GRCh38, whole-genome), gnomad_r2_1 (GRCh37 legacy)

enrich.description: Second-pass fetch gene_symbol, major_consequence, and AF for the top 3 hits.

tools.name: search_variants
tools.description: Use this when a caller uses the legacy tool name -- deprecated alias for resolve_variant_id; returns the same candidates. Mirrors the same enrichment behaviour; will be removed in the next release. Returns ~1-5kB (deprecated alias).

query.description: rsID, CHROM-POS-REF-ALT, or a chrM id (M-POS-REF-ALT).

dataset.description: gnomad_r4 (GRCh38, default, largest cohort), gnomad_r3 (GRCh38, whole-genome), gnomad_r2_1 (GRCh37 legacy)

enrich.description: Second-pass fetch gene_symbol, major_consequence, and AF for the top 3 hits.

tools.name: get_diagnostics
tools.description: Use this when an LLM hits repeated errors or needs server health information; returns recent error history, server version, upstream availability flag, and recent_schema_drift entries so an LLM that hit output_validation_failed can self-diagnose. Returns <1kB.

tools.name: get_server_capabilities
tools.description: Describe this server: allowlisted UCSC tracks per assembly with attribution and terms, coordinate convention, limits, rate-limit policy and error codes. Signature: get_server_capabilities().

tools.name: get_diagnostics
tools.description: Report runtime state without calling UCSC: build, upstream request budget (today's usage vs the daily cap), cache hits, tool latency metrics and live BLAT/isPcr availability per assembly (local gfServer status). Signature: get_diagnostics().

tools.name: list_tracks
tools.description: List the curated UCSC tracks this server can query, with the assemblies each exists on, window limits, provider attribution and terms of use (non_commercial flags SpliceVarDB and Varaico). Signature: list_tracks(assembly=).

assembly.description: Only tracks available on this assembly (default: all).

tools.name: search_genome
tools.description: Find where a gene or transcript lies on an assembly (UCSC position search over MANE, HGNC, GENCODE and RefSeq). Returns 0-based half-open start/end plus a 1-based display string, ready for get_region_annotations. Exact symbol/accession hits come first (`exact_matches` counts them, each hit has `exact`), then UCSC's looser text matches on gene descriptions, which are weak: a disease name is not a gene lookup (resolve it with mondo_resolve_disease). UCSC search gives no strand: get_region_annotations(track='ncbiRefSeqSelect') does. Signature: search_genome(assembly, query, limit=).

assembly.description: Genome assembly: hg38 (=GRCh38) or hg19 (=GRCh37). Never lifted over.

query.description: Gene symbol, transcript accession or term, e.g. BRCA1, SHH, NM_007294.4, ENST00000357654.9.

tools.name: get_region_annotations
tools.description: Return records of one allowlisted UCSC track overlapping a window [start, end) on an explicit assembly: repeats (rmsk, simpleRepeat), segmental duplications (genomicSuperDups), problematic regions (encBlacklist, grcExclusions, GIAB difficult/low-mappability), phyloP, ENCODE cCREs, CpG islands, MANE/GENCODE/RefSeq transcripts, SpliceVarDB/Varaico variants. An empty problematic-region result means the window is not flagged. Native UCSC fields are kept and each record gains a normalized `position`; transcripts also gain `exons` numbered in transcript order (strand-aware), segmental duplications an `other_position` for the partner copy. `total` is exact (null only past the upstream item cap); `truncated` is honest. Windows: <= 2,000,000 bp, signal tracks <= 5,000 bp. Signature: get_region_annotations(assembly, chrom, start, end, track, limit=).

assembly.description: Genome assembly: hg38 (=GRCh38) or hg19 (=GRCh37). Never lifted over.

chrom.description: Chromosome, UCSC style (chr17, chrX, chrM); '17'/'X'/'MT' are accepted.

start.description: 0-based start (first base minus one). 1-based position P is start=P-1.

end.description: 0-based exclusive end (= the 1-based last base). Must be > start.

track.description: UCSC track name from list_tracks. phyloP is phyloP100way on hg38 and phyloP100wayAll on hg19 (either name works on both); cCREregistry/encodeCcreCombined/spliceVarDb are hg38-only.

tools.name: get_reference_sequence
tools.description: Return reference DNA for [start, end) (<= 10,000 bp) on an explicit assembly. Soft-masked: lowercase bases are repeat-masked. strand '-' returns the reverse complement. Signature: get_reference_sequence(assembly, chrom, start, end, strand=).

assembly.description: Genome assembly: hg38 (=GRCh38) or hg19 (=GRCh37). Never lifted over.

chrom.description: Chromosome, UCSC style (chr17, chrX, chrM); '17'/'X'/'MT' are accepted.

start.description: 0-based start (first base minus one). 1-based position P is start=P-1.

end.description: 0-based exclusive end (= the 1-based last base). Must be > start.

strand.description: '+' for the reference strand (default), '-' for reverse complement.

tools.name: find_blat_alignments
tools.description: Return the genomic alignments of one DNA sequence (BLAT, as UCSC web BLAT), i.e. where the sequence comes from. Hits sorted primary assembly first, then by UCSC score, each with 0-based half-open start/end + 1-based display, strand, identity %, query_coverage %, blocks (several blocks = spliced, e.g. cDNA across exons), alt_or_patch for hg38 alt/fix contigs (primary_total excludes them). `total`/`truncated` are honest. Runs on this deployment's own UCSC gfServer; an assembly that is not deployed answers upstream_unavailable (get_diagnostics -> blat shows what is live). Signature: find_blat_alignments(sequence, assembly=, min_identity=, limit=).

sequence.description: DNA, 20-25,000 bases of A/C/G/T/N (other IUPAC codes refused). Whitespace and one optional FASTA header line are ignored; exactly one sequence per call.

assembly.description: Genome assembly (default hg38). Never lifted over.

min_identity.description: Drop hits below this identity % (default 90, gfClient's default).

tools.name: predict_pcr_products
tools.description: Predict every genomic product a primer pair amplifies up to max_product_size (in-silico PCR, as UCSC In-Silico PCR). Each product: location (0-based half-open + 1-based display), size, strand, per-primer mismatch counts and the product sequence (first 1,000 bp; primers uppercase). primary_total counts products off alt/fix contigs (alt_or_patch=true repeats a primary locus): primary_total == 1 is a single genomic product, 0 none. Primers need >= 15 perfect 3' bases. Runs on this deployment's own UCSC gfServer; an assembly that is not deployed answers upstream_unavailable (get_diagnostics -> blat shows what is live). Signature: predict_pcr_products(forward_primer, reverse_primer, assembly=, max_product_size=, limit=).

assembly.description: Genome assembly (default hg38). Never lifted over.

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the GTEx Portal genetic expression database for genes. Accepts a natural-language query (e.g. 'UMOD kidney expression'); gene-like terms are matched against the catalog. Returns result documents with id, title, and URL.

query.description: A natural-language query or gene symbol; gene-like terms are matched against the GTEx catalog (e.g. 'UMOD kidney expression').

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Retrieve full details for a gene from the GTEx Portal database. Use the `id` returned by `search` (`gene:<GENCODE_ID>`); a bare GENCODE ID is also accepted. Expression is listed highest-median tissue first.

id.description: A gene document id from `search` ('gene:<GENCODE_ID>'); a bare GENCODE ID or gene symbol is also accepted (e.g. UMOD).

tools.name: search_genes
tools.description: Search the GTEx Portal gene catalog by gene symbol or partial match. Returns a paginated list of genes with GENCODE IDs, symbols, chromosome, and basic metadata. Use this when the user provides a gene name or partial symbol and you need to disambiguate. Pair with `get_gene_information` for full detail.

query.description: Gene symbol or partial symbol to match against the GTEx catalog (e.g. 'BRCA' matches BRCA1, BRCA2), or an Ensembl gene id. HGNC / NCBI Gene ids are rejected: hgnc_resolve_symbol converts them.

offset.description: Zero-based row offset for pagination (fleet canon).

limit.description: Maximum genes to return per page (1-1000).

tools.name: get_gene_information
tools.description: Retrieve detailed gene information from GTEx Portal for one or more GENCODE IDs or gene symbols. Returns chromosome, coordinates, gene type, Entrez ID, and description. Use when you already know the gene identifier. Inputs that match no gene are listed in `not_found` (`not_returned` when `truncated`); HGNC / NCBI Gene ids are not accepted (`unsupported_identifiers`).

gene_id.description: One or more gene symbols or GENCODE IDs; symbols are auto-resolved (e.g. UMOD or ENSG00000169344.15). For an HGNC or NCBI Gene id, call hgnc_resolve_symbol first.

gencode_version.description: GENCODE annotation release to resolve against; omit for the server default (v26).

genome_build.description: Genome assembly build; omit for the server default. GTEx reference annotations are GRCh38-only, so GRCh37 returns no rows.

tools.name: get_transcript_information
tools.description: Retrieve transcript annotations for a single GENCODE ID from GTEx Portal. Returns transcript identifiers, coordinates, and gene linkage. Use for transcript-level analysis or when the user asks about isoforms.

gencode_id.description: A single VERSIONED GENCODE ID (e.g. ENSG00000169344.15). This tool does NOT auto-resolve gene symbols -- resolve a symbol via get_gene_information or search_genes first.

gencode_version.description: GENCODE annotation release; omit for the server default.

genome_build.description: Genome assembly build; omit for the server default. GTEx reference annotations are GRCh38-only, so GRCh37 returns no rows.

offset.description: Zero-based row offset for pagination.

tools.name: get_median_expression_levels
tools.description: Get median GTEx Portal expression (TPM) per tissue for one or more genes (GENCODE IDs or symbols; symbols are auto-resolved). Results are grouped per gene with invariant fields hoisted. Use `sort` + `top_n` to answer 'where is this gene expressed most?' in one call; `response_mode='full'` adds ontologyId; `include_spread=true` adds per-tissue min/max/quartiles/IQR (one extra upstream call).

gencode_id.description: One or more gene symbols or GENCODE IDs; symbols are auto-resolved to the dataset's GENCODE release (e.g. UMOD or ENSG00000169344.15). At most 18 genes per call.

tissue_site_detail_id.description: A single GTEx tissue, or a list of tissues to compare in one call; omit for all tissues.

sort.description: Order tissues by median expression: desc (highest first, default), asc (lowest first), or none (upstream order).

top_n.description: Keep only the top N tissues after sorting (>=1); omit for all. Pair with sort to answer 'where is this expressed most/least?'.

response_mode.description: compact (default; tissue/median/n only) or full (adds ontologyId per tissue).

include_spread.description: Add per-tissue min/max/quartiles/IQR (one extra upstream call).

offset.description: Zero-based gene offset for pagination.

tools.name: get_individual_expression_data
tools.description: Get individual-sample GTEx Portal expression data (TPM) for one or more genes (GENCODE IDs or symbols; symbols are auto-resolved), optionally filtered by tissue and dataset. Returns one row per gene-tissue; each row's `data` is an unlabeled per-sample TPM vector (no sample/donor IDs, upstream order) with `n` = sample count. NOTE: `limit` paginates the gene-tissue ROWS, not samples -- filter by tissue to bound size. Use for variance/distribution analyses where per-sample data is needed.

gencode_id.description: One or more gene symbols or GENCODE IDs; symbols are auto-resolved (e.g. UMOD or ENSG00000169344.15).

tissue_site_detail_id.description: Restrict to a single GTEx tissue; omit for all tissues (high volume).

offset.description: Zero-based row offset (rows are gene-tissue pairs, not samples).

limit.description: Maximum gene-tissue rows per page; filter by tissue to bound size.

tools.name: get_top_expressed_genes_by_tissue
tools.description: Get the top expressed genes for a given tissue from GTEx Portal. Use when answering 'what's expressed in this tissue?' rather than 'where is this gene expressed?'. Returns genes ranked by median expression.

tissue_site_detail_id.description: The GTEx tissue to rank genes within (e.g. Whole_Blood).

offset.description: Zero-based row offset for pagination.

limit.description: Maximum genes to return per page.

tools.name: get_server_capabilities
tools.description: Return supported tools, datasets, the tissue vocabulary, recommended workflows, response modes, error codes, and limits. Compare `capabilities_version` to skip re-fetching when unchanged.

tools.name: get_server_capabilities
tools.description: Return the hgnc-link discovery surface. detail='summary' (default) is light: identity/build/HGNC release, the tool list WITH call signatures, accepted argument aliases, response modes, recommended workflows, error taxonomy, and limits. detail='full' adds vocabularies (locus groups, status values, match types) and the cross-reference database catalogue. Call this first in a cold session, or read hgnc://tools / hgnc://capabilities. Signature: get_server_capabilities(detail=).

detail.description: summary (default, light) or full (adds vocabularies/xref dbs).

tools.name: get_hgnc_diagnostics
tools.description: Report the local HGNC index status: whether the data is built, the loaded release date, gene/withdrawn counts, schema version, and when it was built. Use this to confirm freshness or diagnose an unavailable-data error. Signature: get_hgnc_diagnostics().

tools.name: resolve_symbol
tools.description: Resolve any gene symbol, HGNC id or external gene id to its canonical record. For 2 or more genes, call resolve_symbols_batch once (up to 200, same accepted forms) instead of calling this tool per gene. Accepts a current symbol, a previous (withdrawn) symbol, an alias, an NCBI Gene synonym HGNC does not list, an HGNC id in either form (HGNC:1100 or 1100), or an Ensembl gene id (ENSG00000157764), RefSeq accession, UniProt accession or NCBIGene:<n> CURIE, case-insensitively. Returns {hgnc_id, approved_symbol, name, status, locus_type, location, match_type (hgnc_id|current|previous|alias|ncbi_synonym|ensembl_gene_id|entrez_id|refseq_accession|mane_select|uniprot_ids)}; an id-type match_type names the external id type that matched; location is the cytogenetic band (chromosome location, e.g. 3p24.3). ncbi_synonym means only NCBI Gene (not HGNC) knows the symbol, and it ranks below every HGNC match. A bare number is always read as an HGNC id, never an NCBI Gene id (write NCBIGene:<n> for that): the result then carries a note, and next_commands offers resolve_gene_by_xref(source='entrez_id'). An alias or synonym shared by several genes returns an ambiguous_query error with the candidate list (not silently picked); a withdrawn/merged symbol returns a not_found error that redirects to the successor record.

query.description: A gene symbol (current/previous/alias), an HGNC id (HGNC:1100 or 1100; a bare number is always an HGNC id), or an external gene id: Ensembl gene id, RefSeq accession, UniProt accession or NCBIGene:<n> CURIE. Case-insensitive.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: resolve_symbols_batch
tools.description: Resolve or translate a batch of gene symbols, HGNC ids and/or external gene ids in one call (max 200). Accepts Ensembl gene ids (e.g. ENSG00000157764), RefSeq accessions, UniProt accessions and NCBIGene:<n> CURIEs, so a list of ENSG ids -> HGNC symbols is one call. Each entry is resolved exactly like resolve_symbol; an individual miss or withdrawal never fails the batch (it is marked unresolved / obsolete in that entry). Returns one row per input in input order (each keeps its input as query, with approved_symbol, hgnc_id, match_type), resolved/unresolved counts, and unresolved_queries (the inputs with no single match). Signature: resolve_symbols_batch(queries, response_mode=).

queries.description: Gene symbols, HGNC ids and/or Ensembl gene / RefSeq / UniProt / NCBIGene:<n> ids to resolve (max 200).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_gene
tools.description: Return the full HGNC record for a gene, resolved from an HGNC id, current symbol, previous symbol, alias, or an external gene id (Ensembl gene id, RefSeq / UniProt accession, NCBIGene:<n>) exactly like resolve_symbol. Includes name, status, locus group/type, location (cytogenetic band), aliases/previous symbols, gene groups, and all cross-references. For a complete alias list read alias_symbol + prev_symbol (HGNC) AND ncbi_gene_synonyms (NCBI Gene's own synonyms, kept separate; may repeat or extend HGNC's). response_mode controls verbosity (compact drops dates/provenance; minimal keeps identity + anchor ids). Signature: get_gene(query, response_mode=).

query.description: A gene symbol (current/previous/alias), an HGNC id (HGNC:1100 or 1100; a bare number is always an HGNC id), or an external gene id: Ensembl gene id, RefSeq accession, UniProt accession or NCBIGene:<n> CURIE. Case-insensitive.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: search_genes
tools.description: Search gene symbols, names, aliases, and previous symbols by free text (FTS); returns relevance-ranked {hgnc_id, symbol, name, locus_type, score} gene summaries. Nomenclature-only: there is NO disease/phenotype semantics, so a descriptive query (e.g. 'polycystin kidney') only matches words present in a gene's nomenclature. Use resolve_symbol for an exact symbol/id; use this for partial names. Signature: search_genes(query, limit=, response_mode=).

query.description: Free-text query (symbol fragment, name, alias).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_gene_cross_references
tools.description: Return external database cross-references for a gene (forward identifier mapping): NCBI Gene, Ensembl, UniProt, RefSeq, MANE Select, OMIM, UCSC, VEGA, CCDS, MGI, RGD, Orphanet, COSMIC, PubMed. response_mode sets the default field set: minimal=NCBI+Ensembl ids; compact (default)=the high-value ids (NCBI, Ensembl, UniProt, RefSeq, MANE Select, OMIM, CCDS); standard/full=every populated field. databases optionally filters to specific sources by field key OR friendly label (e.g. 'mane', 'ncbi', 'uniprot') and OVERRIDES the response_mode tier; an unknown key is rejected with invalid_input + did-you-mean. query takes the same forms as resolve_symbol (symbol, HGNC id, Ensembl gene id, RefSeq / UniProt accession, NCBIGene:<n>). Signature: get_gene_cross_references(query, databases=, response_mode=).

query.description: A gene symbol (current/previous/alias), an HGNC id (HGNC:1100 or 1100; a bare number is always an HGNC id), or an external gene id: Ensembl gene id, RefSeq accession, UniProt accession or NCBIGene:<n> CURIE. Case-insensitive.

databases.description: Optional cross-reference filter: a list of field keys or friendly labels (e.g. 'ncbi', 'ensembl', 'uniprot', 'refseq', 'mane', 'omim', 'ucsc', 'vega', 'ccds', 'mgi', 'rgd', 'pubmed'). Overrides the response_mode tier; an unknown key is rejected with invalid_input + did_you_mean.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: resolve_gene_by_xref
tools.description: Find the HGNC gene(s) for an external database id (reverse identifier mapping); returns the matching gene summaries (hgnc_id, symbol, name). source is the database (entrez_id/ncbi, ensembl_gene_id, uniprot, refseq, mane_select, omim, ucsc, vega, ccds, mgi, rgd) and value is the id (e.g. source='ensembl_gene_id', value='ENSG00000157764'). A version suffix is tolerated (ENSG00000012048.23 resolves like ENSG00000012048), and a MANE Select transcript (ENST…/NM_…) resolves back to its gene. Signature: resolve_gene_by_xref(source, value, response_mode=).

source.description: Cross-reference database. Canonical keys: entrez_id, ensembl_gene_id, uniprot_ids, refseq_accession, mane_select, omim_id, ucsc_id, vega_id, ccds_id, ena, mgd_id, rgd_id. Common synonyms (ncbi, ensembl, uniprot, refseq, mane, omim, mgi, rgd) are also accepted.

value.description: The external identifier value to look up (a version suffix is fine).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_gene_group
tools.description: Browse a HGNC gene group/family by numeric group id (e.g. '1157') or by name (e.g. 'RAF family'). Returns the member genes as symbol-ordered summaries. Members are paginated with limit + offset; the response carries member_count, returned, truncated, and next_offset, and (when truncated) a next_commands entry that fetches the next page. A name matching several groups returns the candidate groups so you can re-call with a specific id. Signature: get_gene_group(group, limit=, offset=, response_mode=).

group.description: Gene group id (numeric) or group name.

offset.description: Skip this many members for pagination (default 0).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_server_capabilities
tools.description: Return the mgi-link discovery surface. detail='summary' (default) is light: identity/build/MGI release, the tool list WITH call signatures, accepted argument aliases, response modes, recommended workflows, error taxonomy, and limits. detail='full' adds vocabularies (allele types, marker types, match types) and the ortholog field catalogue. Call this first in a cold session, or read mgi://tools / mgi://capabilities. Signature: get_server_capabilities(detail=).

tools.name: get_diagnostics
tools.description: Report the local MGI index status: whether the data is built, the loaded release, marker/allele/phenotype/ortholog/disease counts, schema version, and when it was built. Use this to confirm freshness or diagnose a data_unavailable error. Signature: get_diagnostics().

tools.name: resolve_marker
tools.description: Resolve any mouse marker reference to its canonical MGI record. Accepts a mouse symbol (current or synonym, case-insensitive), an MGI id (MGI:98968 or 98968), OR a human gene symbol / HGNC id (resolved to the mouse ortholog). Returns {mgi_id, symbol, name, marker_type, match_type (mgi_id|current|synonym|ortholog)}. An ambiguous symbol returns an ambiguous_query error with the candidate list (not silently picked). A human symbol identical to the mouse symbol resolves as match_type=current (case collision) rather than ortholog; the marker is the same. Signature: resolve_marker(query, response_mode=).

query.description: A mouse marker symbol (current or synonym, case-insensitive), an MGI id (MGI:98968 or 98968), or a human gene symbol / HGNC id / NCBIGene:<id> for the ortholog. A human Ensembl id (ENSG...) is rejected: convert it with hgnc_resolve_symbol first.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_marker
tools.description: Return the full MGI marker record, resolved from an MGI id, mouse symbol/synonym, or human ortholog. Includes name, marker/feature type, GRCm39 location, NCBI/Ensembl ids, synonyms, the human ortholog (symbol/HGNC/OMIM), and summary counts (alleles, phenotypes, phenotype references, diseases). response_mode controls verbosity. Signature: get_marker(query, response_mode=).

query.description: A mouse marker symbol (current or synonym, case-insensitive), an MGI id (MGI:98968 or 98968), or a human gene symbol / HGNC id / NCBIGene:<id> for the ortholog. A human Ensembl id (ENSG...) is rejected: convert it with hgnc_resolve_symbol first.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: search_markers
tools.description: Free-text search over mouse marker symbols, names, and synonyms (FTS, relevance-ranked); returns ranked {mgi_id, symbol, name, marker_type, score, match} summaries. Exact symbol/synonym hits are PINNED first (match: exact_symbol|exact_synonym|fts) so an exact gene is never buried under transgenes or lncRNAs. Returns a truncation contract {total, returned, limit, truncated}; when truncated, next_commands includes a widen step. marker_type optionally restricts to a type (e.g. 'Gene'). Nomenclature-only: no phenotype semantics — use search_phenotype_terms + find_markers_by_phenotype for phenotype-driven discovery, or resolve_marker for an exact symbol/id. Signature: search_markers(query, marker_type=, limit=, response_mode=).

query.description: Free-text query (symbol fragment, name, synonym).

marker_type.description: Optional exact marker-type filter (case-insensitive). One of the MGI marker types; an unrecognised value is rejected with invalid_input.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_marker_alleles
tools.description: Return the phenotypic alleles / mutations for a mouse marker — the gene page's 'All Mutations and Alleles' panel. Includes per-allele {allele_id, symbol, name, allele_type, attributes, pubmed_ids} and the generation-method category_counts (Targeted, Endonuclease-mediated, Radiation induced, Chemically induced, Transgenic, ...). allele_type optionally filters (accepts friendly tokens like 'knockout', 'crispr', 'targeted'). Returns a truncation contract {total, returned, limit, truncated}; when truncated, next_commands includes a widen step. Signature: get_marker_alleles(query, allele_type=, limit=, response_mode=).

query.description: A mouse marker symbol (current or synonym, case-insensitive), an MGI id (MGI:98968 or 98968), or a human gene symbol / HGNC id / NCBIGene:<id> for the ortholog. A human Ensembl id (ENSG...) is rejected: convert it with hgnc_resolve_symbol first.

allele_type.description: Optional generation-method filter. Accepts a canonical MGI allele type or a friendly token (knockout, crispr, cre, enu); an unrecognised value is rejected with invalid_input.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_marker_phenotypes
tools.description: Return the Mammalian Phenotype (MP) annotations for a mouse marker. Distinct MP terms {mp_id, mp_term, genotype_count}, best-supported first; response_mode=full: per-genotype rows with genetic_background, pubmed_id. Paged: {total, returned, limit, truncated}. Single-locus non-conditional genotypes only (scope_note): empty is not absence. Cite via get_server_capabilities. Signature: get_marker_phenotypes(query, mp_system=, limit=, response_mode=).

query.description: A mouse marker symbol (current or synonym, case-insensitive), an MGI id (MGI:98968 or 98968), or a human gene symbol / HGNC id / NCBIGene:<id> for the ortholog. A human Ensembl id (ENSG...) is rejected: convert it with hgnc_resolve_symbol first.

mp_system.description: Optional top-level MP system filter (name or MP id).

limit.description: Max rows — distinct terms, or genotype rows in full mode (default 250).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_phenotype_overview
tools.description: Return a per-system phenotype overview grid: for each top-level MP system annotated for the marker (adipose tissue, cardiovascular system, renal/urinary system, nervous system, neoplasm, vision/eye, ...), the distinct annotated MP terms rolled up via the MP ontology. Use this for the system-level overview, then get_marker_phenotypes(mp_system=) to drill into one system. SCOPE: built from single-locus, NON-conditional genotypes (MGI_GenePheno); conditional/Cre-driven and multi-genic genotypes are EXCLUDED (see the response 'scope'/'scope_note'), so this grid is NOT a full mirror of the MGI gene page and a system may be absent here while the gene page shows it. Signature: get_phenotype_overview(query).

query.description: A mouse marker symbol (current or synonym, case-insensitive), an MGI id (MGI:98968 or 98968), or a human gene symbol / HGNC id / NCBIGene:<id> for the ortholog. A human Ensembl id (ENSG...) is rejected: convert it with hgnc_resolve_symbol first.

tools.name: find_markers_by_phenotype
tools.description: Reverse lookup: return the mouse markers (genes) annotated with a Mammalian Phenotype term. include_descendants defaults to TRUE and changes WHICH genes are returned: it rolls up annotations to more-specific child terms via the MP ontology (e.g. MP:0005367 renal/urinary system phenotype gathers all kidney phenotypes); the flag is echoed in the response. Returns a truncation contract {total, returned, limit, truncated}; when truncated, next_commands includes a widen step. Resolve a term first with search_phenotype_terms. Signature: find_markers_by_phenotype(mp_id, include_descendants=, limit=).

include_descendants.description: Also include child (more specific) MP terms (default true).

tools.name: get_marker_ortholog
tools.description: Return the mouse<->human ortholog mapping and cross-references for a marker: human symbol, HGNC id, NCBI Gene (human), Ensembl (human), OMIM gene id, and human GRCh38 coordinates. Accepts a mouse symbol/MGI id OR a human symbol/HGNC id (resolved to the mouse marker first). Signature: get_marker_ortholog(query, response_mode=).

query.description: A mouse marker symbol (current or synonym, case-insensitive), an MGI id (MGI:98968 or 98968), or a human gene symbol / HGNC id / NCBIGene:<id> for the ortholog. A human Ensembl id (ENSG...) is rejected: convert it with hgnc_resolve_symbol first.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full (default compact).

tools.name: get_marker_diseases
tools.description: Return the human-mouse disease models associated with a marker (Disease Ontology id + name + OMIM ids), from MGI's curated DO annotations. Accepts a mouse symbol/MGI id or a human ortholog. Signature: get_marker_diseases(query).

query.description: A mouse marker symbol (current or synonym, case-insensitive), an MGI id (MGI:98968 or 98968), or a human gene symbol / HGNC id / NCBIGene:<id> for the ortholog. A human Ensembl id (ENSG...) is rejected: convert it with hgnc_resolve_symbol first.

tools.name: get_mp_term
tools.description: Return a Mammalian Phenotype (MP) ontology term: id, name, definition, direct parents and children (is_a edges), and the top-level system(s) it rolls up to. Use with find_markers_by_phenotype to go from a phenotype to the mouse genes that model it. Signature: get_mp_term(mp_id).

tools.name: search_phenotype_terms
tools.description: Free-text search over Mammalian Phenotype (MP) term names and definitions (FTS, relevance-ranked); returns {mp_id, name, definition, score} plus a truncation contract {total, returned, limit, truncated} (widen step in next_commands when truncated). Use this to resolve a phenotype description to an MP id, then find_markers_by_phenotype or get_mp_term. Signature: search_phenotype_terms(query, limit=).

query.description: Free-text phenotype query (e.g. 'small kidney').

tools.name: get_server_capabilities
tools.description: Return the uniprot-link discovery surface. detail='summary' (default) is light: identity/build/release, the tool list WITH call signatures, accepted argument aliases, response modes, recommended workflows, error taxonomy, and limits -- enough to call any tool without guessing an argument name. detail='full' adds the heavy reference blocks (21 named graphs with triple counts, the full SPARQL prefix map, full latency bands, feature-type and cross-reference vocabularies). Call this first in a cold session, or read uniprot://tools (signatures only) or uniprot://capabilities (full). Signature: get_server_capabilities(detail=).

detail.description: summary (default, light) or full (adds named graphs/prefixes).

tools.name: search_sparql_query
tools.description: Run a bounded SPARQL SELECT/ASK query against the UniProt endpoint; returns SELECT results as columns+rows JSON, ASK as a boolean. SERVICE federation and graph-returning CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE forms are rejected. A LIMIT is auto-injected into unbounded SELECTs (see `_meta`/`truncated`). This is the escape hatch for anything the typed tools do not cover -- seed queries from search_example_queries. Use uniprot://prefixes for the standard PREFIX block. Broad, unanchored queries can take 10-60 s; bound lookups (anchored on an accession/gene/taxon) return in <2 s. Signature: search_sparql_query(query, result_format=, limit=, timeout_seconds=).

query.description: A complete SPARQL 1.1 query string. SELECT/ASK only; SERVICE federation and CONSTRUCT/DESCRIBE are rejected. An unbounded SELECT gets an auto-injected LIMIT.
examples:
PREFIX up: <http://purl.uniprot.org/core/>
SELECT ?protein WHERE { ?protein a up:Protein } LIMIT 1

result_format.description: Result serialisation. Use json for SELECT/ASK.

limit.description: LIMIT to inject when a SELECT lacks one (capped at 10000).

tools.name: search_example_queries
tools.description: Search UniProt's 126 curated, executable SPARQL example queries by free text over their descriptions and keyword tags (e.g. 'disease', '3D structure', 'cross-reference', 'taxonomy'). Returns example ids, descriptions, tags, and query types. Fetch the full query text with get_example_query, then run it via search_sparql_query. The best way to learn how to query UniProt. Signature: search_example_queries(text=, limit=).

text.description: Free-text filter over descriptions and keywords.

tools.name: get_example_query
tools.description: Fetch one curated example's full SPARQL text, description, keyword tags, and any federated endpoints it joins. Pass an example_id (full IRI) from search_example_queries. `_meta.next_commands` offers to run it directly via search_sparql_query. Signature: get_example_query(example_id).

tools.name: find_proteins
tools.description: Search UniProtKB for the entries of a GENE and return matching entries (accession, mnemonic, recommended name, reviewed flag, organism). For 2 or more genes, call find_proteins_batch once instead of calling this tool per item. gene_symbol is REQUIRED (a symbol, HGNC:<n> or NCBIGene:<n>; see resolved_from); refine the hits with organism_taxon (a positive NCBI taxon id or an exact common/scientific organism name), reviewed, name_contains (matched per word, in any order, case-insensitive), or the structured filters mnemonic / ec_number / keyword. Reviewed (Swiss-Prot) hits are ranked first. UniProt SPARQL has no general full-text index; for EC-only, keyword-only, or free-text search WITHOUT a gene, use search_example_queries or search_sparql_query. Pair with get_protein for full detail. Results are ordered reviewed-first, then by mnemonic, then accession (stable across pages). Cold search can take several seconds; an identical repeat is cached (~0 ms). If you already know the accession, call get_protein directly -- it is far faster. Signature: find_proteins(gene_symbol, organism_taxon=, reviewed=, keyword=, ec_number=, mnemonic=, name_contains=, limit=, offset=).

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol, HGNC:<n> or NCBIGene:<n>.

organism_taxon.description: Positive NCBI taxon id or exact common/scientific organism name, e.g. 9606, 'human', or 'Homo sapiens'.

reviewed.description: True = Swiss-Prot only; False = TrEMBL only.

keyword.description: UniProt keyword (KW-id like KW-0007, or a label).

name_contains.description: Words to match in the recommended protein name. Multi-word input matches per word (each word must appear, in any order), so 'polynucleotide kinase' matches 'Bifunctional polynucleotide phosphatase/kinase'. Case-insensitive.

offset.description: Pagination offset.

tools.name: find_proteins_batch
tools.description: Resolve SEVERAL gene symbols to UniProtKB entries in ONE call, running the lookups concurrently -- so N genes cost about one cold round-trip instead of N sequential ones. Use this for multi-gene tasks (e.g. 'get domains for PNKP and NAA10'). Returns by_gene (gene -> accessions, reviewed-first), a flat proteins list tagged with matched_gene, resolved_genes, unresolved_genes and unresolved_reasons (not_found, or unsupported_identifier with its converter in next_commands; HGNC:<n>, NCBIGene:<n> accepted; no supported item at all = invalid_input). Optionally scope by organism_taxon (a positive NCBI taxon id or an exact common/scientific organism name) and reviewed. next_commands fan out to get_protein on each resolved gene's top hit. For a single gene use find_proteins. Signature: find_proteins_batch(gene_symbols, organism_taxon=, reviewed=, limit_per_gene=).

organism_taxon.description: Positive NCBI taxon id or exact common/scientific organism name, e.g. 9606, 'human', or 'Homo sapiens'.

reviewed.description: True = Swiss-Prot only; False = TrEMBL only.

tools.name: get_protein
tools.description: Return the core summary for a single UniProtKB entry by accession: mnemonic, reviewed flag, recommended/short name, gene(s), organism + taxon, protein existence, sequence length and mass, a function summary, and creation/modification dates, plus has_variants/has_diseases/has_structure presence flags that drive content-aware next_commands. An obsolete/demerged accession returns a flagged obsolete record (obsolete:true + replaced_by). response_mode (default compact) controls verbosity; standard/full add the created/modified dates. Signature: get_protein(accession, response_mode=).

accession.description: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol / HGNC:<n> / NCBIGene:<n> (resolved to its reviewed entry: resolved_from).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full.

tools.name: get_protein_sequence
tools.description: Return the amino-acid sequence(s) for an entry: the canonical isoform (length, mass, sequence) plus any additional (non-canonical) isoforms. Pass a canonical accession for all isoforms, or an isoform accession (e.g. P05067-2) to get THAT isoform's specific sequence and mass. response_mode controls verbosity: minimal=metadata only; compact (default)=length/mass + a first/last-30-residue sequence_preview (sequence_truncated:true) — cheap for large proteins; standard/full return the complete sequence string. Set canonical_only=true to return only the canonical isoform (skip the additional-isoform list). Signature: get_protein_sequence(accession, response_mode=, canonical_only=).

accession.description: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol / HGNC:<n> / NCBIGene:<n> (resolved to its reviewed entry: resolved_from).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full.

canonical_only.description: Return only the canonical isoform (omit the additional-isoform list).

tools.name: get_protein_features
tools.description: Return sequence features with begin/end coordinates (FALDO) for an entry: domains, regions, transmembrane segments, binding/active sites, PTMs, signal peptides, secondary structure, mutagenesis sites, and more. feature_types=['domain'] returns curated positional domain extents; signature-database domains/families (InterPro/Pfam) are cross-references, pointed to by signature_domain_hint when no domain feature exists. Each returned `type` round-trips to the filter vocabulary. Filter keys come from capabilities (feature_types); a zero-match filter echoes the accepted keys as a filter_hint. Secondary-structure features (helix/strand/turn) are hidden by default and disclosed under excluded_secondary_structure; set include_secondary_structure=true (or name them in feature_types) to return them. DNA-binding extents are not available from UniProt RDF, so dna_binding is deliberately not a filter. response_mode=compact/minimal drops repeated fenced descriptions; standard (default) preserves existing full records. Signature: get_protein_features(accession, feature_types=, limit=, include_secondary_structure=, response_mode=).

accession.description: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol / HGNC:<n> / NCBIGene:<n> (resolved to its reviewed entry: resolved_from).

feature_types.description: Feature-type keys to keep (omit for all). Closed vocabulary: an unrecognised key is rejected (invalid_input), never matched to nothing. See feature_types in get_server_capabilities.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full.

tools.name: get_protein_variants
tools.description: Return natural-variant annotations for an entry: position, wild-type residue, amino-acid substitution, an HGVS-style `notation` (e.g. `L176F`) for simple substitutions, `variant_type` (substitution|other), free-text description, structured linked `diseases`, and `dbsnp` rsIDs. Set disease_associated_only=true to keep only disease-linked variants. Set position_start and/or position_end to keep annotations that overlap that residue interval (inclusive). response_mode=compact/minimal drops the repeated free-text provenance; standard (default) preserves the existing full records. Signature: get_protein_variants(accession, limit=, disease_associated_only=, response_mode=, position_start=, position_end=).

accession.description: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol / HGNC:<n> / NCBIGene:<n> (resolved to its reviewed entry: resolved_from).

disease_associated_only.description: Return only variants linked to a disease.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full.

position_start.description: First residue of an inclusive overlap interval.

position_end.description: Last residue of an inclusive overlap interval.

tools.name: get_protein_diseases
tools.description: Return disease annotations associated with an entry: disease name, UniProt disease id, mnemonic, MIM id, the clinical `definition` (the disease vocabulary's own description), and `involvement` (the entry-specific note). Pairs with get_protein_variants for variant-level disease evidence. response_mode=compact/minimal drops the free-text definition/involvement; standard (default) preserves them. Signature: get_protein_diseases(accession, response_mode=).

accession.description: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol / HGNC:<n> / NCBIGene:<n> (resolved to its reviewed entry: resolved_from).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full.

tools.name: get_protein_cross_references
tools.description: Return database cross-references for an entry, grouped by database (PDB, AlphaFoldDB, Ensembl, RefSeq, Reactome, STRING, InterPro, ...). Optionally restrict to specific databases (case-sensitive); any requested name that matched nothing is echoed under unmatched_databases with a did-you-mean, so a typo never reads as 'no data'. response_mode (default compact) returns short ids; full restores raw IRIs. Returns every cross-reference database; use resolve_identifiers for a focused primary-id mapping. Signature: get_protein_cross_references(accession, databases=, response_mode=).

accession.description: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol / HGNC:<n> / NCBIGene:<n> (resolved to its reviewed entry: resolved_from).

databases.description: Database short names to keep (case-sensitive; omit for all). A malformed name is rejected (invalid_input); a well-formed name that matched nothing is echoed under unmatched_databases.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full.

tools.name: get_protein_go_terms
tools.description: Return Gene Ontology annotations for an entry, grouped by aspect (biological_process / molecular_function / cellular_component) where available, each with GO id, label, and (when annotated) ECO `evidence` ids plus mapped GO `evidence_codes` (IDA/IEA/IMP/...) for citation. Always returns `count` and `count_by_aspect`; pass `aspect` to scope to one ontology and `limit` to cap a large set (token economy). Signature: get_protein_go_terms(accession, aspect=, limit=).

accession.description: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol / HGNC:<n> / NCBIGene:<n> (resolved to its reviewed entry: resolved_from).

aspect.description: Restrict to one GO aspect (omit for all).

tools.name: resolve_identifiers
tools.description: Resolve a UniProtKB accession to its PRIMARY external identifiers: the genomic/structural/family core (PDB, AlphaFoldDB, Ensembl, RefSeq, GeneID, HGNC, KEGG, OrthoDB, Pfam, InterPro) by default. Optionally restrict to specific databases. Returns ids grouped by database plus the databases that matched and per-database counts. response_mode (default compact) returns short ids; full restores raw IRIs. For the exhaustive cross-reference set (incl. drug/disease databases like DrugBank/ChEMBL/OpenTargets) use get_protein_cross_references instead. Signature: resolve_identifiers(accession, databases=, response_mode=).

accession.description: UniProtKB accession, e.g. P05067 (isoforms like P05067-2 accepted), or a human gene symbol / HGNC:<n> / NCBIGene:<n> (resolved to its reviewed entry: resolved_from).

databases.description: Target database short names (case-sensitive; omit for the primary set).

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full.

tools.name: get_taxon
tools.description: Resolve an organism in the UniProt taxonomy. Pass a numeric NCBI taxon id (e.g. 9606) for full detail (scientific/common name, rank, the DIRECT parent, and an optional ordered lineage from species up to root), or a scientific/common name to get candidate taxon ids. Use the resolved taxon id with find_proteins(gene_symbol=..., organism_taxon=...). Name matches are ranked best-first (an exact scientific/common-name hit leads, tagged match_quality:'exact'), so matches[0] and next_commands point at the right organism. Numeric-id and common-organism-name lookups are fast (~0 ms for common names); an uncommon name triggers a multi-second taxonomy scan. Signature: get_taxon(taxon, include_lineage=).

taxon.description: NCBI taxon id (digits) or a scientific/common name.

include_lineage.description: Include the ancestor lineage (id lookups only).

tools.name: get_server_capabilities
tools.description: Get this server's capabilities: supported tools, ClinGen datasets + per-domain snapshot freshness, recommended workflows, token-cost hints, error taxonomy, parameter conventions, and the capabilities_version content hash. Returns ~4kB.

tools.name: search_genes
tools.description: Resolve a free-text gene (symbol / HGNC id / alias) to its canonical ClinGen gene; returns resolved_symbol plus candidates with per-domain availability and record counts. Use this FIRST, before any gene-keyed tool. Follow the _meta.next_commands into get_gene_summary. Unknown input returns a not_found envelope with a fallback. Returns ~1-3kB.

query.description: Gene symbol, HGNC id, or alias to resolve (e.g. BRCA1, HGNC:1100).

tools.name: get_gene_summary
tools.description: Use this for a one-call cross-domain overview of a gene: validity classifications by disease, dosage haplo/triplo scores, actionability adult/pediatric, and ERepo variant counts. Resolve free text with search_genes first. The _meta.next_commands drill into each domain tool. Returns compact ~3-8kB (minimal ~0.5kB).

gene_symbol.description: Canonical gene symbol or HGNC id (resolve with search_genes first).

response_mode.description: minimal = headline + counts only; compact (default) trims verbose fields; standard keeps nulls; full returns every field.

tools.name: get_gene_validity
tools.description: List ClinGen gene-disease validity assertions for one gene; returns per disease the classification (Definitive…Refuted), MONDO id, mode of inheritance, expert panel, classified date, CGGV permalink and recommended_citation. Returns ~1-6kB.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol or HGNC id (resolve with search_genes first).

classification.description: Filter to one ClinGen validity classification.

moi.description: Filter to one mode of inheritance.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims verbose fields; full keeps everything.

tools.name: search_validity
tools.description: Use this to search ClinGen gene-disease validity by disease text/MONDO, expert panel, classification, MOI, or gene. Paginated; a `truncated` block appears when more matches exist. Each record carries a recommended_citation. Returns ~2-10kB.

expert_panel.description: Substring of the curating expert panel name.

moi.description: Filter to one mode of inheritance.

gene_symbol.description: Restrict to one gene symbol.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims verbose fields; full keeps everything.

tools.name: get_gene_dosage
tools.description: Use this for ClinGen dosage sensitivity of a gene: haploinsufficiency + triplosensitivity score with plain-English interpretation, GRCh37/GRCh38 coordinates, disease/MONDO, and PMIDs. Resolve free text with search_genes first. Returns ~1-3kB.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol or HGNC id (resolve with search_genes first).

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims verbose fields; full keeps the PMID lists.

tools.name: search_dosage
tools.description: Search ClinGen dosage-sensitivity curations of genes and recurrent CNV regions (ISCA) by gene, ISCA region id, MONDO id, cytoband, or haplo/triplo score; returns per record its haploinsufficiency + triplosensitivity scores with interpretation, cytoband, GRCh37/GRCh38 coordinates and permalink. Optionally restrict to gene or region records. Paginated; a `truncated` block appears when more matches exist. Returns ~2-10kB.

query.description: Gene symbol / HGNC id, ISCA region id, MONDO id, or cytoband prefix. Disease and syndrome names are not indexed: pass their MONDO id.

haplo_score.description: Exact ClinGen haploinsufficiency score CODE (not its description): 0 no evidence, 1 little, 2 some, 3 sufficient evidence; 30 gene associated with an autosomal-recessive phenotype; 40 dosage sensitivity unlikely; -1 will not be evaluated. -1, 30 and 40 are flags, not evidence levels.

triplo_score.description: Exact ClinGen triplosensitivity score CODE (same scale as haplo_score). Absent scores match no code; -1 marks genes that will not be evaluated.

record_type.description: Restrict to gene or region records.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims verbose fields; full keeps the PMID lists.

tools.name: get_gene_actionability
tools.description: Use this for ClinGen clinical actionability of a gene: adult/pediatric assertion status, release, disease, and SEPIO links. Set include_detail=true to fetch the live SEPIO assertion document for the chosen context. Resolve free text with search_genes first. Returns snapshot ~1-4kB; include_detail adds the live SEPIO payload.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol or HGNC id (resolve with search_genes first).

include_detail.description: Fetch the live SEPIO assertion document for each curation in the requested context (extra upstream calls). False (default) returns snapshot rows.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims SEPIO IRIs; full keeps everything.

tools.name: search_actionability
tools.description: Use this to search ClinGen clinical actionability by disease text or gene. Paginated; a `truncated` block appears when more matches exist. Each record carries the actionability permalink + recommended_citation. Returns ~2-8kB.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol that the curation lists.

context.description: Seed the citation with this assertion context.

assertion.description: Curation status of the adult OR pediatric assertion to filter by (e.g. 'Released'). A value outside the enum is rejected by validation.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims SEPIO IRIs; full keeps everything.

tools.name: get_variant_interpretations
tools.description: Use this to list ClinGen ERepo expert-panel variant interpretations by gene, disease (disease text/MONDO), expert panel, or classification. Returns each variant's CAID, canonical HGVS, MONDO, ACMG classification, VCEP, dates, and permalink. Drill into one with get_variant_interpretation. Paginated. Returns ~2-12kB.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol (resolve with search_genes first).

expert_panel.description: Substring of the curating VCEP name.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims evidence-code/PubMed lists; full keeps them.

tools.name: get_variant_interpretation
tools.description: Use this for the full ACMG interpretation of one expert-panel variant: evidence codes Met / Not Met, the classification outcome, guideline/CSpec, PubMed evidence, and the permalink. variant_id takes a CAID, a ClinVar VariationID, or an HGVS expression. refresh=true bypasses the snapshot for the live SEPIO JSON. Returns ~2-8kB.

variant_id.description: The variant to look up, in any ONE of the three identifier shapes ERepo keys on: a ClinGen Allele Registry id (CA003783), a ClinVar VariationID (17662), or an HGVS expression (NM_007294.4:c.68_69del). The shape is detected from the value.

refresh.description: Bypass the snapshot and fetch the live SEPIO interpretation.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims verbose blocks; full keeps every field.

tools.name: list_cspecs
tools.description: Use this to browse ClinGen criteria-specification (CSpec) headers, filtered by gene, curating affiliation (VCEP), or lifecycle status. Each row carries the GN id, affiliation, label, version, and status. Drill into one with get_cspec. Paginated; returns ~1-8kB.

gene_symbol.description: Gene symbol or HGNC id covered by the spec.

affiliation.description: ClinGen affiliation id of the curating VCEP.

status.description: CSpec lifecycle status filter (cspecStatus). A value outside the enum is rejected by validation.

response_mode.description: compact (default) drops nulls + verbose header fields.

tools.name: get_cspec
tools.description: Use this for one criteria specification in full: its genes/diseases, every ACMG/AMP criterion with strength rules, and the attached guidance files. Resolve a gn_id first with list_cspecs (by gene, affiliation, or status). Returns ~3-30kB depending on the spec.

gn_id.description: CSpec GN identifier. Resolve one from a gene, an affiliation (VCEP) or a status with list_cspecs, whose rows carry the gn_id.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims verbose header fields; full keeps them.

tools.name: get_cspec_criterion
tools.description: Use this for a single CSpec criterion's specification: its ACMG/AMP code, description, the VCEP's strength rules, and any attached evidence files. Addressed by its natural key — the specification (gn_id) plus the ACMG/AMP code — with rule_set_id only for a code a spec defines twice. Returns ~1-4kB.

gn_id.description: CSpec GN id (from list_cspecs / get_cspec / search_cspec).

rule_set_id.description: Only needed for the few codes a spec defines in more than one rule set; the ambiguous_query error names it and lists the rule sets.

response_mode.description: compact (default) trims nulls; full keeps every field.

tools.name: search_cspec
tools.description: Search the ClinGen criteria-specification (CSpec) catalog full-text across spec labels, criteria descriptions, and attachment filenames; returns matching specs, criteria, and files. Each hit names its entity_type + ids so you can chain into get_cspec or get_cspec_criterion. Paginated; returns ~1-6kB.

query.description: Full-text query across spec labels, criteria, and filenames.

tools.name: list_expert_panels
tools.description: Use this to list ClinGen GCEP/VCEP expert panels (affiliates) with their curation counts, optionally filtered by label text. Useful to resolve an expert-panel name before filtering validity or variant interpretations. Returns ~1-5kB.

query.description: Filter by expert-panel label text (FTS).

tools.name: get_diagnostics
tools.description: Use this when an LLM hits repeated errors or needs server health information; returns recent error history, server version, snapshot freshness, and recent_schema_drift entries so an LLM that hit output_validation_failed can self-diagnose. Returns <1kB.

tools.name: get_server_capabilities
tools.description: Return the GenCC-Link tool inventory, classification vocabulary and ranks, response modes, recommended workflows, error codes, resources, and live data freshness. Compare `capabilities_version` to skip re-fetching when unchanged.

tools.name: get_gencc_diagnostics
tools.description: Report build provenance and data freshness: GenCC run date, source ETag/last-modified, row/gene/disease/submitter counts, schema version, and when the local database was built. Also echoes server_version and capabilities_version so a warm client can poll this small payload for drift instead of re-fetching the full capabilities document.

tools.name: search_genes
tools.description: Search the GenCC gene catalog by approved symbol, partial symbol, or HGNC id. Returns ranked genes with assertion roll-ups (number of diseases, submitters, strongest classification, conflict flag). Use to resolve free text before get_gene_curations. Page large result sets via the release-bound truncated.next_cursor (surfaced as _meta.next_commands[0]).

query.description: Gene symbol, partial symbol, or HGNC id to search for. An Ensembl or NCBI Gene id is rejected with the call that converts it.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact.

limit.description: Rows per page (1-200; above 200 is clamped).

offset.description: Zero-based row offset for paging.

cursor.description: Opaque, release-bound page token from a prior truncated.next_cursor.

tools.name: get_gene_curations
tools.description: Single-gene lookup: returns all GenCC gene-disease validity assertions for ONE gene, grouped by disease, each with a consensus classification across submitters and a conflict flag. Identify the gene with gene_symbol (an approved symbol OR an HGNC CURIE). For several genes in one call use get_genes_curations (plural). Widen response_mode for the per-submitter breakdown. Page via the release-bound truncated.next_cursor (surfaced as _meta.next_commands[0]).

gene_symbol.description: Gene identifier: an approved HGNC symbol (e.g. SKI) or an HGNC CURIE (e.g. HGNC:10896). Exact match; resolve free text with search_genes first. An Ensembl or NCBI Gene id is rejected with the call that converts it.

response_mode.description: Verbosity: minimal | compact | standard | full.

limit.description: Rows per page (1-200; above 200 is clamped).

offset.description: Zero-based row offset for paging.

cursor.description: Opaque, release-bound page token from a prior truncated.next_cursor.

tools.name: get_genes_curations
tools.description: Multi-gene batch: returns the asserted diseases (consensus classification + conflict flag) for a LIST of up to 20 gene symbols or HGNC ids in one call; for a single gene use get_gene_curations (singular). Unresolvable inputs come back in `unresolved` and the call still succeeds. Each result block mirrors get_gene_curations (gene summary + consensus diseases). Use limit_per_gene to cap diseases per gene and response_mode to widen detail.

genes.description: Gene symbols or HGNC ids (max 20). An Ensembl or NCBI Gene id is listed under `unsupported`, with the call that converts it.
