Signature: get_molecular_profile(molecular_profile_id).

tools.description: Return one CIViC variant: coordinates with their assembly (CIViC's primary build is GRCh37), genomic HGVS labelled GRCh37/GRCh38, transcript HGVS, MANE Select HGVS, ClinGen CAID, ClinVar IDs, variant types (SO) and its single-variant molecular profile. Signature: get_variant(variant_id).

Signature: search_assertions(molecular_profile_id=, disease=, therapy=, assertion_type=, amp_level=, status=, response_mode=, limit=, offset=).

therapy.description: NCIt code (C64768, exact) or therapy name (Vemurafenib, matches CIViC names containing it); unknown is not_found.

response_mode.description: minimal: IDs + classification | compact (default): + disease, therapies, profile, source | standard/full: + fenced curator text.

tools.name: get_assertion
tools.description: Return one assertion: type, direction, actionability (AMP tier/level, FDA companion test, regulatory approval, NCCN guideline) or oncogenicity / germline_pathogenicity with their codes, DOID disease, therapies, the fenced summary and description, and the evidence items behind it (status, level, molecular profile, PMID). Signature: get_assertion(assertion_id).

assertion_id.description: CIViC assertion ID as a number or 'AID10'.

tools.name: get_gene
tools.description: Return a CIViC gene (symbol, full name, NCBI Gene ID, aliases, fenced curator summary) and the variants CIViC curates for it, each with its single-variant molecular profile ID; `total` is exact, page with offset. Ensembl or HGNC IDs are rejected with a converter step. Signature: get_gene(gene, limit=, offset=).

gene.description: HGNC symbol (BRAF) or NCBI Gene ID (NCBIGene:673).

offset.description: Rows to skip; use the previous `next_offset`.

tools.name: get_gene_alteration_frequency
tools.description: Get how often a gene is altered per cBioPortal study: mutation (altered / profiled samples, panel-aware), optional protein_change (e.g. KRAS G12C) and CNA (amplified / deep-deleted / profiled), each row with licence, citation and import_date. Pick studies by cancer_type (OncoTree code, subtypes included, largest first, max_studies; total/truncated count matching studies) or study_ids; neither = MSK-IMPACT 2017 pan-cancer. tools.name: search_approvals
tools.description: Search MOAlmanac regulatory approvals of biomarker-directed cancer therapies (FDA, EMA, Health Canada, Ireland HSE/HPRA). One row per agency statement: agency, status (Approved/Accelerated), biomarkers, genes, disease (NCIt, OncoTree), therapies, label document, version date and regulatory ID. Filters combine with AND; an unknown value is not_found naming it, with the closest names. Empty = no MOAlmanac approval found, not 'not approved'. `summary` counts agencies, regimens and biomarkers (co-occurring ones too) over all matches. 'Wild type X' rows are eligibility criteria, not X-targeted drugs. Rows hit by a known upstream error carry `known_defects`. Signature: search_approvals(gene=, biomarker=, disease=, therapy=, agency=, biomarker_type=, response_mode=, limit=, offset=).

gene.description: Gene symbol (ERBB2; aliases HER2, PD-L1), HGNC ID, Ensembl or NCBI Gene ID.

biomarker.description: Biomarker words, e.g. 'BRAF V600E', 'G12C', 'v::ALK' (fusions are 'v::GENE', any partner; V600 also matches V600E/K); an exact list_biomarkers name matches only that biomarker, and 'NOT <name>' the rows that require its absence.

disease.description: Disease name words (melanoma), or an OncoTree (NSCLC) or NCIt code as MOAlmanac records it; subtype codes (LUAD) are not mapped to parents.

biomarker_type.description: Only rows with a biomarker of this type (of `gene`, if given): 'Gene fusion' keeps ALK fusions and drops 'Wild type ALK' rows.

response_mode.description: minimal: ids, agency, biomarkers, therapies, label date | compact (default): + genes, disease codes, label | standard: + label URL, predicate, strength | full: + fenced indication text.

limit.description: Max rows (default 20, max 100); 0 = only total and summary.

offset.description: Rows to skip; use the previous `next_offset`.
